phase.instructions: The state is the latest slice of a coding agent's session transcript (user messages, assistant text, tool calls with one-line results, diffs). Which work phase does this slice show the agent in right now? Judge the most recent activity, not the whole task.

criteria.planning: Reading code, exploring, designing an approach, writing a plan or brief, deciding scope; no production edits yet
criteria.implementing: Editing or writing production code or config, wiring features, mechanical changes; edits are landing
criteria.verifying: Running tests, typechecks, builds, smoke runs, or checking output of the changed path; results mostly pass or are being read
criteria.debugging: Investigating a failing test, error, crash, or wrong output: reproducing, reading stack traces, trying fixes in response to failures
criteria.blocked: Cannot proceed: missing access, credentials, environment, a decision only the user can make, or the same failure repeating without a new idea
criteria.reporting: Summarizing what was done, presenting evidence, writing changelog/PR text, answering the user; no further tool work in progress

needs_review.instructions: A senior advisor model watches this coding agent's session and can interject with critique or a course correction. Invoking it costs a full model call. Should the advisor be invoked on THIS transcript slice right now, whether the agent is mid-task or has just yielded? Yes only when the advisor can materially catch or improve something: a landed code change or design decision, a claim that work is done or fixed (especially without visible evidence), a risky or destructive command, a repeated failure or stuck loop, a change of direction, or a question to the user that deserves a second opinion. No when nothing would change by reviewing it: greetings, small talk, banter, a short factual answer, an acknowledgement, routine reads and searches, a single passing check, small mechanical edits, or in-flight work with nothing decided yet.

criteria.true: The advisor can act on this slice now: a decision, landed change, completion claim, repeated failure, risky action, deviation, or an open question worth a second opinion
criteria.false: Nothing for the advisor to act on: chit-chat, a short answer, routine exploration, or mechanical progress

progress.instructions: How much forward progress does this transcript slice show compared with what it was trying to do? Consider whether tool calls produce new information or landed changes, whether the same command or edit keeps repeating, and whether errors are being resolved or recurring.
criteria: Advancing: each step yields new information or a landed change; errors, if any, are resolved and not repeated
Churning: some progress but effort is going into retries, reformulations, or edits that get reverted; the same error or command appears more than once
Stuck: the same failure or command repeats with no new idea, the agent circles between two approaches, or it explicitly says it cannot proceed

done_without_evidence.instructions: Does the assistant in this transcript slice claim the task is done, fixed, implemented, passing, or ready WITHOUT showing evidence in the same slice: no test or command run whose result supports the claim, no observed output, only assertion?

criteria.true: A completion claim is present and no supporting command output, test result, or observation appears
criteria.false: No completion claim, or the claim is backed by visible command output, test results, or an observed run

parallel_slices.instructions: Does the work in this transcript slice contain two or more independent pieces that could be done at the same time by different people, each with its own files and its own check? Independent means neither piece needs the other's output first.

criteria.true: Two or more separable work packages with distinct files or components and no runtime dependency between them
criteria.false: One coherent slice, sequential steps that depend on each other, or work too small to split
